history.dynasty: Late medieval (one web source attributes the present structure to 1585 under Raja Puran Mal; unverified and possibly conflated with Baidyanath Temple)
history.period: Ancient shrine; present structures medieval to modern (dating disputed)
history.summary: Baba Basukinath Dham is the famous Shiva temple of Basukinath town, Dumka district, about 42-46 km from Deoghar on the Dumka-Deoghar road (CSV town 'Deoghar' is imprecise; corrected here). Tradition holds that a pilgrimage to Baidyanath Dham is incomplete without darshan at Basukinath - 'Devghar ka Kachari, Basukinath ka Diwani' (petitions are filed at Deoghar, the hearing happens at Basukinath). Legends: a villager named Basu found the lingam while digging; alternatively Nagraj Vasuki did penance here after the Samudra Manthan and Shiva stayed on as 'Basukinath'. Some local belief calls it a Jyotirlinga, though it is not in the canonical Dwadash list. The Ghatwals of Nonihat feature in its history; the Van Ganga pond nearby is used for ritual bathing. Distance from Deoghar varies across sources (42 km, 45 km, 46 km).

name: Baba Basukinath Dham
town_description: Basukinath (also called Basukinathdham) is a temple town in Jarmundi block of Dumka district in the Santhal Pargana division, on the Dumka-Deoghar road. The settlement grew around the famous Baba Basukinath Dham Shiva shrine.

travel.railway: Jasidih Junction and Dumka are the nearest major railway stations
travel.road: On the Dumka-Deoghar road, ~42-46 km from Deoghar and ~25 km from Dumka

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Shravani Mela (July-August) is the festival peak
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opens ~4 AM, closes ~8 PM (sources conflict: deoghar.co says 3 AM opening; verify locally)
